title: Measure Sydney Airport's cap on the hour and set curfew noise standards
action: Amend the law so the 80-movements-an-hour cap is measured over clock hours rather than rolling 15-minute windows, and replace the named freight aircraft allowed in the curfew with a noise standard, without raising noise or the number of curfew movements.
why: The rolling measure leaves usable capacity idle and the aircraft-type rule blocks quieter modern freighters, both raising costs at Australia's busiest airport without protecting residents any better.

evidence.quote: The Australian Government should amend section 6(2) of the Sydney Airport Demand Management Act 1997 (Cwlth) to define a regulated hour as a period of 60 minutes starting on the hour.

The Australian Government should amend the Sydney Airport Curfew Act 1995 (Cwlth) to introduce noise standards for freight aircraft allowed during the curfew, rather than specifying only one type of freight aircraft (the British Aerospace 146).
